newsitem.title: UK: Britain should show support for European FLA -MPs.
newsitem.headline: Britain should show support for European FLA -MPs.

text.p: Britain should make a gesture of support for a project for a new huge cargo plane to be built by Airbus Industrie, parliament's Defence Committee said on Thursday.

It said in a report that the Future Large Aircraft project currently on the drawing board could result in huge orders for Britain's aerospace industry if it promised to order the aircraft for its forces.

The report said provided a Defence Ministry study currently being undertaken showed the need for a strategic airlift of heavy military equipment, the government "should not delay" in seeking further information from Airbus, including the price.

"Such a move would not commit the Government in any way to future purchases but would nonetheless demonstrate a degree of commitment to our European partners on defence collaboration and would help to ensure that the option of future purchases of the FLA is kept open," it added.
The FLA is one of the options Britain is exploring for the replacement of part of its ageing fleet of 55 Hercules C-130 transport aircraft built by Lockheed Martin Corp.

Other possibilities are to order McDonnell Douglas C-17s or to replace the whole fleet with an updated version of the Hercules. Some 25 of the new Hercules have already been ordered as the first tranche of the replacement programme.

The share of the work on the FLA among the industries of participating countries would be based on the number of aircraft each country ordered. Spain, France and Germany have already given initial indications of support for the FLA. The committee said that British Aerospace Plc had told it that if Britain had a 20 percent share, this would be worth between three and six billion stg to Britain's aerospace industry.

"We urge the Government to give careful consideration to industrial considerations when reaching a decision on the second tranche of the Hercules replacement programme," its report said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
